piątek, 8 marca 2024 o 10:51:18 UTC+1 Adrian Wysocki napisał(a):
Dear DarR Community,

I am currently conducting research involving sequencing data from a specific species of moss (haploidal organism). I am reaching out to seek your expertise and guidance in resolving an issue I have encountered during the analysis of the sequencing data I have received.

Upon review, I noticed that the sequencing data provided is formatted for a diploidal organism, I have attached screenshots illustrating this issue for your reference.

I am wondering if there is a possibility to transform this data to align with the characteristics of a haploidal organism. Are there any tools or methods that you could recommend for this purpose? Any assistance or insights you could provide would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you very much for considering my request. Your support and guidance in this matter would be immensely valuable to the progress of my PhD project.

Warm regards,
Adrian Wysocki

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Ploidy problem
parts:
Hi Adrian,

You can check the R package poppr (Poppr: an R package for genetic analysis of populations with clonal, partially clonal, and/or sexual reproduction [PeerJ]). 
See code below, for an example.

library(dartR)
library(poppr)
t1 <- platypus.gl
t1 <- gl.filter.allna(t1)
# check function documentation
?make_haplotypes
t2 <- make_haplotypes(t1)


Cheers,
Luis
